summary: safeGit now catches git failures and returns a GitResult object with code, stdout and stderr instead of a string. index.ts also re-exports the GitResult type.

findings.title: Return type change breaks both CLI callers
findings.problem: safeGit now resolves to a GitResult object instead of a string. The callers still call string methods on it, namely trim() in packages/cli/src/branch.ts:7 and split() in packages/cli/src/status.ts:7.
findings.consequence: In currentBranch, the TypeError from trim is caught, so the function always returns null. The CLI then always prints not a git repository and exits with code 1.
findings.fix: Update both callers to read result.stdout. Have currentBranch return null when result.code is not 0.

findings.title: Swallowed failure removes the not-a-repository signal
findings.problem: safeGit no longer throws when git fails. currentBranch at packages/cli/src/branch.ts:8 relies on a throw to return null outside a repository.
findings.consequence: If currentBranch is changed only to read stdout, it will return an empty string outside a repository instead of null. The CLI would then report a blank branch instead of an error.
findings.fix: Have every caller check result.code and handle a non-zero exit explicitly. currentBranch should return null when the code is not 0.

findings.title: New failure path has no covering test
findings.problem: No test covers the new GitResult return shape or the catch branch that maps execFile errors to code. The change added no tests.
findings.consequence: Mapping regressions for non-numeric error codes, such as ENOENT, would go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests that cover a successful git call, a failing git call and a missing git binary.
